extDescription.message: Vertical tabs as a tree in the side panel. Tabs you open from a page nest under it, and you can drag them to reorganize.
extDescription.description: The extension's description on chrome://extensions and in the Chrome Web Store. At most 132 characters. Lead with the words people search for, like "vertical tabs".

actionTitle.description: Tooltip of the extension's toolbar button, which opens the tree in the side panel. "Tree of Tabs" is the extension's name: keep it in English.

commandDescription.description: Name of the keyboard shortcut on chrome://extensions/shortcuts. "The tree" is the tree of tabs in the side panel.

pinnedTabs.description: Screen reader name for the row of pinned tabs at the top of the panel.

tabs.description: Screen reader name for the tree of tabs.

newTab.description: Button under the tree, and a menu item: opens a new tab. Use Chrome's own words for "New tab".

newTabTooltip.message:
New tab
Middle-click: new tab under the current tab
newTabTooltip.description: Tooltip of the "New tab" button, on two lines. A middle click opens the new tab nested under the tab that's open now.

untitledTab.description: Shown for a tab that has no title yet. Chrome's own title for a blank new tab, so use Chrome's words.

closeTab.description: Screen reader name of the X button on each tab.

expand.description: Tooltip of the arrow on a tab whose children are hidden: shows them again.

collapse.description: Tooltip of the arrow on a tab with children: hides its children in the tree.

muteTab.description: Button and menu item: mutes this tab's sound.

unmuteTab.description: Button and menu item: turns this tab's sound back on.

muteTabs.description: Menu item when several tabs are selected: mutes them all.

unmuteTabs.description: Menu item when several tabs are selected: turns their sound back on.

windowTipTitle.message: Each window has its own side panel.
windowTipTitle.description: Bold first sentence of a one-time tip at the top of the panel; the rest of the tip is windowTipShortcut.

windowTipShortcut.message: $TITLE$ Chrome doesn't let extensions open it by themselves, so in a new window, show the tree with the toolbar button or $SHORTCUT$.
windowTipShortcut.description: A one-time tip at the top of the panel, shown the first time the tree opens while several windows are open. The first placeholder is the tip's bold first sentence (windowTipTitle), the second the keyboard shortcut. "It" is the side panel. The toolbar button is the extension's button in Chrome's toolbar.

title.example: Each window has its own side panel.

windowTip.message: $TITLE$ Chrome doesn't let extensions open it by themselves, so in a new window, show the tree with the toolbar button.
windowTip.description: The same as windowTipShortcut, for when the user removed the keyboard shortcut.

title.example: Each window has its own side panel.

gotIt.description: Button that closes the tip for good.

fullscreenTitle.message: Hide the tree during full screen?
fullscreenTitle.description: Title of a one-time question shown in the panel the first time a page goes full screen.

fullscreenIntro.message: Chrome keeps the side panel open next to full screen videos and pages. Tree of Tabs can close it when you go full screen.
fullscreenIntro.description: First paragraph of the full screen question. "Tree of Tabs" is the extension's name: keep it in English.

fullscreenReopenShortcut.message: Chrome doesn't let extensions reopen the side panel by themselves, so afterwards you bring the tree back with the toolbar button or $SHORTCUT$.
fullscreenReopenShortcut.description: Second paragraph of the full screen question. The toolbar button is the extension's button in Chrome's toolbar. The placeholder is the keyboard shortcut.

fullscreenReopen.message: Chrome doesn't let extensions reopen the side panel by themselves, so afterwards you bring the tree back with the toolbar button.
fullscreenReopen.description: The same as fullscreenReopenShortcut, for when the user removed the keyboard shortcut.

hideDuringFullscreen.description: Main button of the full screen question: the panel closes whenever a page goes full screen.

keepItOpen.description: Other button of the full screen question: the panel stays open during full screen.

changeLaterInSettings.message: You can change this later in Settings.
changeLaterInSettings.description: Small note under the full screen question's buttons.

newTabAsChild.description: Menu item on a tab: opens a new tab nested under this tab.

newTabUnderCurrent.message: New tab under the current tab
newTabUnderCurrent.description: Menu item of the "New tab" button: opens a new tab nested under the tab that's open now.

reload.description: Menu item: reloads the tab. Use Chrome's own word from its tab menu.

duplicate.description: Menu item: opens a copy of the tab. Use Chrome's own word from its tab menu.

pin.description: Menu item: pins the tab. Use Chrome's own word from its tab menu.

unpin.description: Menu item: unpins the tab. Use Chrome's own word from its tab menu.

expandTree.description: Menu item: shows the hidden children of this tab again.

collapseTree.description: Menu item: hides the children of this tab in the tree.

collapseAll.description: Menu item: hides the children of every tab in the window.

expandAll.description: Menu item: shows every hidden tab in the window again.

indent.description: Menu item: makes the tab a child of the tab above it, one level deeper.

outdent.description: Menu item: moves the tab one level up, out of its parent.

moveToNewWindow.description: Menu item on a tab without children: moves it to a new window.

moveTreeToNewWindow.description: Menu item on a tab with children: moves it and all its children to a new window.

moveTabsToNewWindow.description: Menu item when several tabs are selected: moves them to a new window.

closeChildren.description: Menu item: closes the tabs nested under this tab, and keeps this tab.

closeTree.description: Menu item: closes this tab and every tab nested under it.

closeTabs.description: Menu item when several tabs are selected: closes them.

closeOtherTabs.description: Menu item: closes every other tab in the window except pinned ones. Use Chrome's own words from its tab menu.

closeTabsBelow.description: Menu item: closes the tabs below this one in the tree, except pinned ones. Like Chrome's "Close tabs to the right", but the tree is vertical.

settings.description: Menu item: opens the extension's settings page.

settingsPageTitle.description: Title of the settings page, shown on its browser tab. "Tree of Tabs" is the extension's name: keep it in English.

newTabsHeading.description: Heading of the settings about opening tabs.

placeTabs.message: Place tabs opened from a tab
placeTabs.description: Setting: where a tab opened from another tab goes among that tab's children.

placeTabsHint.message: Links, middle clicks and pages that open tabs
placeTabsHint.description: Explains what "tabs opened from a tab" means.

asLastChild.description: Choice for where new child tabs go: below its other children.

asFirstChild.description: Choice for where new child tabs go: above its other children.

newTabAsChildSetting.message: Open new tabs (Ctrl+T) as children of the current tab
newTabAsChildSetting.description: Setting, on or off: blank new tabs nest under the tab that's open.

newTabAsChildHint.message: Off: blank new tabs start their own tree
newTabAsChildHint.description: What happens when the setting is off.

closingTabsHeading.description: Heading of the settings about closing tabs.

whenParentClosed.message: When a parent tab is closed
whenParentClosed.description: Setting: what happens to a tab's children when that tab is closed.

promoteFirst.description: Choice: the first child takes the closed tab's place, and the other children move under it.

promoteAll.message: Move all children up a level
promoteAll.description: Choice: every child moves up one level.

closeAllChildren.description: Choice: the children close together with the parent.

closeCollapsedTree.message: Close the whole tree when its collapsed parent is closed

closeCollapsedTreeHint.message: Hidden tabs close with the parent you can see
closeCollapsedTreeHint.description: Explains the setting: the tabs hidden inside a collapsed tree close too.

appearanceHeading.description: Heading of the settings about how the tree looks.

density.description: Setting: how much space each row takes.

indentation.description: Setting: how far each level of children is moved to the right.

hideGuideLinesHint.message: The thin lines from each tab down to its children. Tab group colors still show.
hideGuideLinesHint.description: Explains what the guide lines are.

turnOffCollapsing.description: Setting, on or off. Also quoted in notAvailableWhile, so keep the two the same.

turnOffCollapsingHint.message: Removes the arrows and the collapse options, and keeps every tree expanded

autoExpand.message: Expand a collapsed tree when one of its tabs is selected

autoExpandHint.message: For example when switching tabs with Ctrl+Tab

hideInFullscreen.message: Hide the tree when a page goes full screen

hideInFullscreenHint.message: For example a video. Chrome doesn't let extensions reopen the side panel by themselves, so bring it back afterwards with the toolbar button or its keyboard shortcut.
hideInFullscreenHint.description: Explains the setting. The toolbar button is the extension's button in Chrome's toolbar.

advancedNote.message: These change how Chrome itself normally behaves.

keepWindow.message: Keep the window open when its last tab is closed from the tree

keepWindowHint.message: Chrome normally closes a window together with its last tab. With this on, closing the last tab from the tree opens a new tab first, so the window stays open. Closing it with the keyboard shortcut or from the tabs at the top of the window still closes the window, as usual.
keepWindowHint.description: Explains the setting. "The tabs at the top of the window" is Chrome's own tab strip.

notAvailableWhile.description: Note on a setting that's turned off because another setting is on. Use the quotation marks of your language.

notNeededCloseAll.message: Not needed: closing a parent already closes its children
notNeededCloseAll.description: Note on "Close the whole tree when its collapsed parent is closed" when "Close its children too" is chosen.

sidePanelTip.message: Tip: Chrome can show the side panel on the left. Open $LINK$ and set $SETTING$ to $VALUE$.
sidePanelTip.description: Tip at the bottom of the settings page. The placeholders are a link to Chrome's appearance settings and the names of a Chrome setting and its value.

chromeSidePanelPosition.description: The name of a setting on Chrome's own appearance settings page. Must be exactly Chrome's words in your language.

chromeShowOnLeft.description: A value of Chrome's "Side panel position" setting, on its appearance settings page. Must be exactly Chrome's words in your language.

feedback.message: Found a bug? $REPORT$. Have an idea? $SUGGEST$.
feedback.description: Line at the bottom of the settings page. The placeholders are two links: reportIt and suggestFeature.

madeBy.message: Tree of Tabs is made with care by Lawand, an independent developer.
madeBy.description: About the developer, at the bottom of the settings page. Keep the names as they are.

macApps.message: If you like keeping your tabs organized, you might like Taskbar, my app for switching between windows on the Mac.
macApps.description: Shown only on a Mac. "Taskbar" is the name of an app: keep it in English.

discover.message: Discover my other software at $SITE$, and follow $ACCOUNT$ on X.
discover.description: The placeholders are links to a website and an account on X.
